subject: ventures/vinyl-liner-bid-calculator
professional: a pool service contractor who replaces residential inground vinyl liners (measures the pool to a manufacturer's liner measuring form, orders the custom liner, drains, sets, vacuums and refills). First checks: is the liner area right for the deep-end geometry (shallow depth, deep depth, hopper/slope dimensions), does a measured liner area flow through to the material order, and are drain/refill and repair allowances in the price.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python recomputation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/8306f0fd-c968-539e-b9ee-e65b62b706c7/scratchpad/indep.py) from first principles (rectangle 2(L+W), ellipse area pi*a*b, ellipse perimeter by numerical integration rather than the author's Ramanujan formula, margin = profit/price) with the page's default rates: 16x32 hopper preset liner 960.64 sf, 23.59 h, cost 3,989.84, price 5,319.79; 18x36 oval preset perimeter 87.196 lf (exact integral) vs tool 87.196 (Ramanujan), price 9,946.52 vs tool 9,946.51 (one cent, the Ramanujan approximation). All four presets solve to exactly 25.00% margin on price. The arithmetic engine is right. Held at 2 because two outputs a contractor acts on are wrong or unsupported: (1) the page's derived geometry chain goes stale: an edited liner sf (e.g. the manufacturer's measured figure) never updates order sf, so liner material does not change (engine run: linerSf 960.64 -> 1200 leaves linerMaterial 1,919.36); and orderSf is always rebuilt from the suggested, not the edited, liner sf (index.html:454,463). (2) The hopper extra is a flat 22% of water surface regardless of deep-end depth; an independent heightfield model of a 16x32 hopper (3.5 ft walls, 1:1 to 1:1.5 hopper sides) gives 11-15% extra at 6.5 ft deep and 15-20% at 8 ft, so 22% sits at or above the top of the envelope and cannot respond to depth. Blank numeric fields silently become 0 (calculateBid({...linerSf:''}) -> 0).
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked: shape/depth/mil/bead/stairs/pattern/access kits (work, engine run), liner sf/order sf/price stack (works), walk-away price and proposed-price verdict (2,999 against the 16x32 preset -> belowBreakEven true, profit -990.84), copy bid summary (formatBidSummary, tested), share link round trip incl. proposal terms (share.test.mjs, proposal-terms.test.mjs pass), proposal print panel (proposal.test.mjs), usage tally with opt-out/DNT/GPC (usage.test.mjs). Three marketing pages present and linked from llms.txt. No TODOs or stubs found. Limitations section honest about commercial, vinyl-over-concrete, structural scope.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/vinyl-liner-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 134/134 pass, 0.24 s. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: hopper 0.22->0.20 caught; track hours not scaled by perimeter caught; Ramanujan term changed caught; wall-foam material not scaled by perimeter SURVIVED; stair labour dropped from liner share of direct cost SURVIVED; break-even comparison < -> <= SURVIVED. 3 of 6 survived, including a real price component (foam material) and one of the two headline decision numbers the VENTURE.yaml hypothesis names (liner share of direct cost). page.test.mjs is string-matching on HTML (no DOM), so the stale derived-field behaviour is untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (574 lines), index.html script (lines 366-720), page.test.mjs header, proposal-terms.test.mjs. Engine is pure, deterministic, strict on unknown preset ids and on yes/no words, escapes nothing it does not need to. Defects: derived fields (water -> walls -> liner -> order) are independent inputs with no recomputation when an intermediate is edited, so the page can price an internally inconsistent takeoff; Number('') -> 0 accepted for every numeric field; proposal-terms.test.mjs:137 uses a water-heater payload ('heaterType=tankless&location=attic&gallons=50'), a sign the shared terms module and its tests were copied from another venture.
evidence.claims: vs-a-flat-2999-special.html: 512 vs 508.94 sf water, $5,319.79 vs $9,946.51, 1.87x: all reproduced independently (5,319.79; 9,946.52; 1.870). README:31 '96 lf of wall, about 961 sf of liner on a 512 sf floor': 96 and 336 sf wall check by hand; 961 depends on the uncited 22% hopper factor (partial). Margin-vs-markup FAQ claim correct (25% markup clears 20% margin). vs-jobber.html: Jobber founded 2011, Edmonton, no price invented (pass). Rates (liner $1.85/2.85/3.35 per sf, hours per 100 sf, track $8.50/lf, cover $480) are uncited but the README (line 75) and page label them as editable ballpark starting figures, not quotes. Disclaimer on page footer (index.html:333) and README; usage tracking present. Served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) rewrites llms.txt to marisstella.app with no placeholder left; the duncan-haywood.github.io links in source llms.txt are source-only.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: 16x32 hopper, enter spans, pick 20 mil, compare a 2,999 coupon -> walk-away 3,989.84, clear 'loses $990.84' verdict, copyable summary and printable proposal. A contractor gets a usable first price. Gaps hit in the first hour: no deep-end depth input, so the hopper liner area cannot be set from the pool's actual measurements without overriding the hopper field by hand; typing the measured liner area from the manufacturer's form does not change the material order; no water refill/trucked water or volume-based drain time (pump-down is a flat 2.5 h whether 15k or 33k gallons; 16x32 at ~5 ft average depth is 512*5*7.48 = 19,149 gal); no floor/wall repair allowance (only mentioned in the proposal disclaimer).
evidence.domain: Compared with manufacturers' liner measuring practice (inground liner measuring forms ask for length, width, shallow depth, deep depth, and the hopper/transition distances, and the liner is fabricated to them) and with the trade's line items (drain, remove, floor and wall repair, new bead/track, set, vacuum, refill with water and chemicals). Departs: deep-end depth absent, hopper extra a flat percentage of water surface; pump-down hours independent of volume; refill water and startup chemicals not modelled; repair allowance absent. Margin-on-price math, wall = perimeter x wall height, ellipse geometry and pattern waste uplift are standard.

defects.what: Derived takeoff goes stale: editing liner sf (e.g. the manufacturer's measured area) never updates order sf, so liner material and price do not change; order sf is always rebuilt from the suggested liner sf, not the edited one, and editing wall/hopper/stair sf does not update liner sf. The page prices an internally inconsistent takeoff without warning.

Hopper extra is a flat 22% of water surface with no deep-end depth input; an independent floor model gives 11-20% depending on depth and slope, so the figure is at or above the top of the range and cannot respond to a 6.5 ft vs 8 ft deep end, which manufacturers' measuring forms require.
Blank numeric fields silently become 0 (Number('') === 0): clearing order sf or liner $/sf drops liner material from the price with no error.
Wall-foam material scaling by perimeter is untested: replacing perimeterLf * foamPerLf with foamPerLf leaves all 134 tests green.
Liner share of direct cost (a headline decision number per VENTURE.yaml) is untested: dropping stair labour from it survives; the break-even boundary (< vs <=) also survives.
No water volume, drain time or refill: pump-down is a flat 2.5 h for any pool and there is no refill water/trucked water or startup chemical line, items a liner replacement bid normally carries.
Liner $/sf by mil, hours per 100 sf, track $/lf and other starting rates are uncited (labelled ballpark only).
README claim 'about 961 square feet of liner' rests on the uncited 22% hopper factor without saying so.
Test fixture copied from a water-heater venture ('heaterType=tankless&location=attic&gallons=50').

verdict: The arithmetic engine is correct: an independent recomputation reproduces every preset price to the cent (the oval to one cent, from Ramanujan vs an exact ellipse integral) and margin is solved on price. It falls short of a liner contractor's sign-off on two things a reader can check: the page does not carry an edited liner area through to the material order (index.html:463), and the hopper liner area is a flat 22% of water surface with no deep-end depth, where manufacturers' measuring forms start from shallow and deep depths. Three of six seeded mutants survived, including the wall-foam material line. Finished (completeness 3), below the bar (correctness 2, verification 2).
